dimensions.note: No secrets. Swamp logins (token usernames or OAuth subs) are kept on person data, which every reader already sees; the app still calls no site, and the egress tests pass over the new code.
app_step logs which login took which step as whom, and whoami who a login is. Round 1 found login changes unlogged; add_person and update_person now say the swamp login set or cleared.

Refusals are DomainErrors in people's words: not on the list, no login, service logins, a stand-in, a taken login, a version not named, a build path. The app shows a step's error from the run's completed event.

77 tests pass. New tests cover the whole app flow as two logins, refusal of unknown, service and ghost logins, one login per person, none on a stand-in, a login taken away, build paths and JSON for another request, whoami without a nonce, and logins through a snapshot (failing without the collision rule). Checked by hand under swamp serve with token logins in a browser: raise, submit, join, reply, agree, refusals.

Raise sends one idempotency key per form, so a retry logs one request. The dashboard broker forwards no idempotencyKey on a workflow run, so the README says a step that lost its connection may have been taken. The same build result or router test twice changes nothing, as before.

The workflow has no input naming who acts; principal comes only from run.initiatedBy, which serve sets from the signed-in principal, and the broker refuses ${{ in an app's inputs (tested that the workflow has no as or principal input). app.yaml runs only that workflow and no methods.
Each app open writes one small signedIn record; each step is one run whose stream ends with it. Nothing is held open.

Round 1 found the README's user:alice only right for token sign-in; it now says the login is the user:<id> serve records, the token username or the OAuth sub, and that the refusal names it. It warns against granting run on the requests behavior, says steps need the behavior named capture, that a lost step may have been taken, and that the app doesn't start stand-ins. The stale 'There is no sign-in' line is reworded.
Logins match user:<id> on add, update and import; step is an enum, nonce a short regex, every text capped. Anything but an exact user: login on the list is refused.
signedIn is kept 1d with GC 1: it is read at once and only needed while the app is open.
A login is set on add_person, changed or cleared (blank) on update_person, exported and imported with its person.
The login is matched before any method runs; Record build's path and request checks run before reading anything; Agree needs a version of 1 or more.

signed-in-<nonce> takes a random UUID per open. Round 1 found another runner could write the same name once seen; the app now accepts the record only if its workflowRunId tag is the run it started (checked under serve). The app refuses steps when it shows a behavior other than capture, the one the workflow acts on.

The app reads with data:read and writes only by the step workflow, as the run's own login. An import carries logins only where no one here holds them, counts both, and the README says a login means someone only to the serve that signed them in.
All three behavior types go to 2026.11.27.1 with no-op upgrades; the new optional principal field and signedIn resource need no migration. The manifest's version matches.
